patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches depict a feedback-style form with multiple text input fields beneath explanatory copy and no other obvious interactive widgets. The mobile sketch shows three stacked inputs; the desktop sketch shows two side-by-side inputs plus another field below, implying a submit-ready form that needs validation.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Inputs should validate on submit at minimum, and likely on blur/input for common checks such as required fields and email formatting. Validation should account for the responsive layout difference between stacked mobile fields and multi-column desktop fields.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not explicitly mark required fields, show a submit button, or indicate exact validation rules; however, a production form implementation would still require validation behavior.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a very low-JS page: primarily a responsive informational form with standard text inputs and no visible navigation, overlays, expandable sections, tabs, search, or dynamic loading. The main cross-viewport difference is layout only—mobile stacks fields vertically while desktop places some fields side by side—so the only clearly necessary JavaScript pattern is form validation with accessible focus/error handling.
